messages:
maya: Quick design review — canary traffic stepper + version carousel iteration. Pushing updated Figma link: https://www.figma.com/file/xxx. Quick thumbs and accessibility nits please :eyes: joel: Nice. First thought — canary increments look like 1, 5, 25, 100. Can we make the step labels more descriptive? 'tiny p50 ramp' is confusing for PMs maya: Good point. Thinking labels: 1% (smoke), 5% (small canary), 25% (gradual), 100% (full). Short copy under the stepper? sam: Also need to think about how batching affects latency. If users pick 1% we might route to smaller pool. Should be fine but add tooltip: 'may affect tail latency' aria: Accessibility: keyboard + screenreader concerns for the version carousel. Right now it's a carousel with no focus trap. Need arrow-key navigation and aria-live region when preview changes. oliver: Agree. I'll add tabindex handling and announce "Previewing vX — diff summary". Also suggest adding role="listbox" and role="option" on items. maya: For rollback action — current CTA is 'Undo rollout'. That sounds ambiguous. Propose 'Rollback to previous version' and a secondary 'Rewind with traffic ramp' option joel: +1. Also need to clarify risk level in modal. Add 'estimated user impact' and 'expected recovery time' snippets. aria: Modal must not rely on color alone. Use icons + text: 'High risk' 'Low risk'. Ensure focus lands on first actionable button and trap until dismissed. oliver: Small code snippet for aria-live: ```
Preview: v2.3.4 — 12 lines changed
``` oliver: Also recommend `aria-roledescription="version carousel"` on the container. maya: The version carousel also needs a compact view for mobile — suggestion: vertical stack with swipe gestures. Thoughts? sam: Perf wise, the carousel preloads diffs for adjacent versions only. Good for memory. aria: Test notes: VoiceOver reads the aria-roledescription but announce count is noisy. Maybe compress announcement: 'Version 3 of 7: preview loaded'. joel: UX question: Should users be able to simulate traffic split locally? A 'dry run' toggle could show how traffic moves without committing. maya: Love that. Add a 'Dry run' toggle next to stepper with tooltip 'Preview traffic distribution without applying'. deploy-bot: Snapshot generated for preview: https://app.preview/redwood/preview/9876 :white_check_mark: oliver: I'll push a prototype with keyboard nav and updated copy by EOD Tuesday. maya: Can the copy be 1) 'Rollback to previous version' 2) 'Rewind and ramp traffic' and tooltip examples? Also include microcopy under stepper 'Select how quickly this variant should receive traffic.' sam: I'll review the impacts and add a note in the deployment docs about queueing and batching. aria: I'll run NVDA/VoiceOver pass on the prototype when ready. Tag me when PR is up :mag: maya: Thanks team — will iterate on Figma and post updated link. :thumbsup:
